evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-order-repository.ts: class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository, so it is an adapter for a domain port (persistence).
save() and findById() only read and write a private Map<string, Order>, which is storage logic.
findByStatus() filters stored orders by status equality. That is a query, not a business rule.
nextId() hands out sequential IDs ('order-N'), which is an identity-generation detail of the storage.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file passes. It is a pure persistence adapter: an in-memory store that implements the domain OrderRepository port. Generating IDs with nextId, storing orders with save, fetching them with findById and filtering them with findByStatus are all storage and query tasks that belong in an infrastructure layer. findByStatus only compares order.status to the status passed in. It does not decide when a status is valid, allowed or changed, so it carries no business rule. The file has no domain invariants, no application orchestration and no business decisions.
